title: Government Launches Nationwide Digital Literacy Mission
subtitle: New initiative aims to bring one million citizens online with free training centres in every district.
description: A sweeping new public initiative was unveiled today to expand digital literacy across rural and urban districts alike, with training centres planned in over 600 locations nationwide.
content: The Ministry of Digital Affairs announced a nationwide Digital Literacy Mission on Thursday, aiming to train more than one million citizens in basic computer and internet skills over the next three years.
Officials said the programme will prioritise rural districts, women, and senior citizens, with free training centres opening in over 600 locations by the end of the year.
"This is about giving every citizen the tools to participate in the digital economy," the minister said at the launch event, flanked by state education officials and technology partners.
The mission will be delivered through a mix of physical training centres and a mobile app offering self-paced lessons in twelve regional languages.

Independent analysts welcomed the announcement but cautioned that past digital-inclusion programmes have struggled with last-mile delivery in remote areas. The ministry says it has built in quarterly public progress reports to address that concern.
author: Editorial Desk

title: Parliament Passes Clean Energy Amendment Bill
subtitle: The bill sets a binding target of 50% renewable capacity by 2032.
description: Lawmakers approved sweeping amendments to the national energy framework, setting binding renewable-capacity targets for the next decade.
content: The lower house passed the Clean Energy Amendment Bill after an extended debate, setting a binding target of 50 percent renewable generation capacity by 2032.
The legislation introduces tax incentives for rooftop solar adoption and creates a new regulatory body to fast-track transmission projects.
Opposition lawmakers supported the bill's goals but raised concerns about implementation timelines and funding for grid modernisation.
The bill now moves to the upper house, where it is expected to be taken up next month.
author: Ritu Sharma

title: Global Leaders Meet to Address Supply Chain Resilience
subtitle: Representatives from 40 nations discuss coordinated response to shipping bottlenecks.
description: A two-day summit brought together trade ministers from forty countries to discuss strengthening global supply chains after repeated disruptions.
content: Trade ministers from forty nations convened this week to discuss a coordinated approach to strengthening global supply chains.
The summit's closing statement called for shared early-warning systems for shipping disruptions and greater investment in regional manufacturing hubs.
Several delegates emphasised the need to reduce dependency on single-source suppliers for critical goods such as semiconductors and pharmaceuticals.
A follow-up meeting is scheduled for early next year to review progress on the commitments made.
author: Foreign Desk

title: Central Bank Holds Interest Rates Steady Amid Inflation Watch
subtitle: Policymakers cite easing inflation but caution on global headwinds.
description: The central bank's monetary policy committee voted to keep rates unchanged, citing a gradual cooling in inflation.
content: The central bank's monetary policy committee voted unanimously to hold the benchmark interest rate steady, citing signs that inflation is gradually cooling.
In its statement, the committee said it would continue to monitor global commodity prices and currency fluctuations before considering further moves.
Market analysts had largely expected the decision, with most forecasting no change until at least the next quarterly review.
Business groups welcomed the stability, saying it would help firms plan investment with greater confidence.
author: Business Desk

title: Researchers Unveil Low-Cost Water Purification Device
subtitle: The solar-powered unit could serve remote communities lacking clean water access.
description: A team of university researchers has developed a solar-powered water purification unit designed for off-grid communities.
content: A team of engineers has unveiled a solar-powered water purification device designed to serve communities without reliable access to clean water.
The device uses a combination of UV filtration and a low-cost membrane system, and can be manufactured locally for a fraction of the cost of comparable imported units.
Field trials are set to begin in three states later this year, with support from a public health partnership.
Researchers say the technology could be adapted for disaster-relief deployment as well as permanent rural installations.
author: Tech Desk

title: National Team Clinches Regional Championship in Thrilling Final
subtitle: A last-minute goal sealed the title after a hard-fought match.
description: The national team secured the regional championship title with a dramatic late goal in front of a capacity crowd.
content: The national team claimed the regional championship after a tense final that was settled by a goal in the closing minutes.
Fans packed the stadium to capacity, with celebrations continuing well into the night across several cities.
The coach praised the squad's resilience, noting that the team had come from behind twice during the tournament.
Attention now turns to the upcoming qualifiers, where the squad will look to build on this momentum.
author: Sports Desk

title: International Film Festival Opens With Record Number of Entries
subtitle: Over 300 films from 45 countries will screen across the ten-day event.
description: This year's film festival opened with a record 300-plus entries from 45 countries, reflecting growing global interest.
content: The festival opened Thursday evening with a record 300-plus film entries submitted from 45 countries.
Organisers said the growth reflects rising interest from independent filmmakers seeking wider distribution.
The ten-day event will feature panel discussions, workshops, and a new category dedicated to short documentaries.
Award winners will be announced at a closing ceremony next weekend.
author: Arts Desk

title: Coastal Cities Expand Flood-Resilience Infrastructure Projects
subtitle: New drainage and wetland-restoration projects target chronic monsoon flooding.
description: Several coastal cities have begun new flood-resilience infrastructure projects ahead of the monsoon season.
content: Municipal authorities in several coastal cities have broken ground on new flood-resilience projects, including expanded drainage networks and wetland restoration.
The projects are designed to reduce chronic flooding that has disrupted transport and commerce during recent monsoon seasons.
Environmental groups praised the wetland-restoration component in particular, noting its dual benefit for flood control and biodiversity.
Officials say the first phase of projects should be complete before next year's monsoon.
author: Environment Desk

title: New Public Health Campaign Targets Preventive Care
subtitle: Free screening camps to be held in 200 towns over the next two months.
description: A new public health campaign will offer free preventive-care screenings in 200 towns over the coming two months.
content: Health authorities launched a preventive-care campaign that will bring free screening camps to 200 towns over the next two months.
The camps will offer basic health checks, including blood pressure, blood sugar, and vision screening, at no cost.
Officials hope early detection will reduce long-term treatment costs and improve outcomes for common chronic conditions.
Mobile health units will supplement fixed camps in areas with limited clinic access.
author: Health Desk

title: University Launches Major Scholarship Programme for First-Generation Students
subtitle: The fund will cover full tuition for 5,000 students annually.
description: A leading public university has launched a scholarship fund aimed at supporting first-generation college students.
content: A major public university announced a new scholarship fund that will cover full tuition for 5,000 first-generation students each year.
The fund, backed by a mix of alumni donations and government matching grants, will also provide mentorship and career-placement support.
University officials said the programme responds to research showing that financial barriers remain a leading cause of college dropout.
Applications for the first cohort open next month.
author: Education Desk

title: Startup Ecosystem Report Shows Record Early-Stage Funding
subtitle: Early-stage investment rose 28% year-on-year, led by fintech and agri-tech.
description: A new industry report finds early-stage startup funding reached a record high this quarter, led by fintech and agri-tech sectors.
content: Early-stage startup funding climbed 28 percent year-on-year this quarter, according to a new industry report, led by strong activity in fintech and agri-tech.
Investors said improving macroeconomic conditions and a wave of first-time founders from tier-two cities contributed to the growth.
The report also flagged a rise in follow-on funding, suggesting greater investor confidence in scaling existing portfolio companies.
Analysts expect the momentum to continue into the next quarter, barring global market shocks.
author: Business Desk

title: City Metro Network Adds Two New Lines, Cutting Commute Times
subtitle: The expansion connects three previously underserved suburbs to the city centre.
description: Two new metro lines opened this week, connecting underserved suburbs to the city centre and cutting average commute times.
content: Two new metro lines opened to the public this week, extending the network into three previously underserved suburbs.
Transport officials estimate the expansion will cut average commute times for affected residents by up to 40 minutes daily.
The project, which took four years to complete, also included accessibility upgrades at twelve existing stations.
A third line is currently under construction and expected to open within two years.
author: Editorial Desk
